source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events?release=manufacturing-business-outlook-survey, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 131,089 bytes) by the philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15 initial research, whose embedded release calendar lists 'September Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey' on Sep 17 2026 at 8:30 a.m. Corroborated on the same domain by the MBOS landing page (philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/regional-economic-analysis/manufacturing-business-outlook-survey, HTTP 200 the same day), whose next-releases block reads 'Sep 17 2026 September Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey 8:30 a.m.' verbatim, and independently reproduced by the survey's third-Thursday cadence: September 2026's Thursdays are the 3rd, 10th, 17th and 24th, so the third is the 17th. Filed estimate on the two standing counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-08. It is filed for a measured reason and not for series completeness: TWO ledgers already on the shelf name this exact date as a kill switch, and the calendar tracks it nowhere. empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15.md's kill-switch list reads 'Empire and Philly September prices paid converge inside ~5 points (2026-09-15 / 2026-09-17)', and philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15.md registers two forward tests whose anchors this print resets. A date that existing research has already elevated to a decision trigger is exactly what a calendar is for. Two further reasons it is not merely the next edition of a low-impact series. First, it is 9 days out and lands INSIDE the 30-day low:15+ reassessment interval of the October ledger, whose next scheduled pulse is 2026-10-08 — so without a row of its own it would be met 21 days stale. Second, its own morning is materially readable where 10-15's is not: the calendar's 2026-09-17 slate is housing starts (low), pending home sales (low), Eurostat HICP final (low), a 10-year TIPS auction and a coupon announcement, with no Census or BLS major sharing the 8:30 minute, against 10-15's retail sales (high) plus PPI (medium). It also falls on the LAST day of the FOMC's September blackout — the Philadelphia Fed's own calendar page lists the 2026 blackout windows verbatim as 'September 5-17' and 'October 17-29', which is a Federal Reserve primary for both dates. Impact LOW and symbols [] on the same grounds as the October entry: the Third District footprint (Delaware, southern New Jersey, eastern and central Pennsylvania) is sub-state, the headline explains ~27% of national manufacturing IP growth since 2001, and no house playbook is keyed to regional surveys. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and whoever writes the canonical philly-fed-mfg-2026-09-17.json owns re-verifying the date.
